decisions.evidence: Round 4 Maker: 'Paste `https://fortelabs.com/blog/basboverview/` into the web-address field and select Add link. You should see the title, description, site name, icon, and image gathered for review before anything is saved.' Round 4 Client: 'One field at the top where I paste and hit "Add link," then it shows me what it found before saving — that's exactly the kind of flow I was hoping for. And it did pull in all the things I care about: the title, the little description, the site name and its icon, and a picture.'
decisions.note: Prototype review stage. Saving a bookmark by entering a URL and automatically collecting target page metadata (title, description, favicon, preview image) conforms to REF-BM-01 and REF-BM-02.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 Maker: 'You should see the title, description, site name, icon, and image gathered for review before anything is saved... but for now stop at the preview and tell me what you think.' Round 4 Client: 'One thing I noticed on that "Here's what we found" step: it's showing me the details, but I can't touch them... So on that review step, before I hit save, I'd want to be able to fix up the title or the description myself. And ideally I could still tweak them later too, after it's saved, if I change my mind.'
decisions.note: Prototype review stage. The preview step before saving presented auto-collected details as read-only, diverging from REF-BM-03. The client identified the mismatch and supplied the requirement to edit the title and description in place before saving (and after saving).

decisions.evidence: Round 5 Maker: 'Reload http://maker:4001, add the same sample link, then change its title on the review step to “My PARA reference.” Stop before saving and tell me whether editing the gathered details there feels right. I’ve assumed the title and description are directly editable in place'. Round 5 Client: 'Yes, this is exactly right. On the review step the title and description are both mine to change — I can type right over them... I made the title "My PARA reference" and it stuck on the saved card.'
decisions.note: Prototype review stage. Editable title and description directly in place on the review step before saving conforms to REF-BM-03.

decisions.evidence: Rounds 6-8 Maker: presents three comparable entry points for post-save editing (Option A: clear Edit button, Option B: ••• menu -> Edit details, Option C: hover pencil). Round 8 Client: 'I'll go with the "•••" menu (option B)... That little menu feels like the natural home for all of those, editing included, without cluttering the card.'
decisions.note: Prototype review stage. Post-save editing conforms to REF-BM-04; the choice among entry mechanisms (Edit button, ••• menu, hover pencil) is a functionally equivalent UI choice.

decisions.evidence: Round 9 Maker: 'use the bookmark’s ••• → Edit details, and type this into My note: `Use this when I reorganize my research folder.` Then save it. I’ve assumed notes belong in the same editing screen as the title and description, and that a saved note appears directly on the card for quick recognition.' Round 9 Client: 'One thing I'd want as these notes grow: sometimes my note is more than a single sentence. I might want a couple of bullet points, or to make a word or two stand out, or drop in a link. So I'd like to be able to give the note a little basic formatting and have it actually show up formatted when I look at the card or the bookmark — not just come out as one flat run of text.'
decisions.note: Prototype review stage. Personal notes were presented as unformatted flat plain text, diverging from REF-BM-23. The client extended the scope by requesting basic formatting (bullets, emphasis, links) rendered when viewing.

decisions.evidence: Round 11 Maker: 'The saved card behavior is unchanged; only the way formatting is entered differs... Tell me which approach you prefer afterward.' Round 11 Client: 'Having seen both, I prefer the first one — the toolbar with the B, italic, bullet, and link buttons... it asks me to type little symbols — the stars and dashes and bracket things — to get the formatting, and I'd have to learn and remember what each one does. I'm not that kind of person; I just want to select a word and click a button to make it bold... So: go with the toolbar approach for entering it, and keep that clean formatted result on the card.'
decisions.note: Prototype review stage. REF-BM-23 specifies writing markdown notes on bookmarks. The client explicitly recognized that Option B required typing markdown syntax ('stars and dashes and bracket things') and accepted the departure by choosing the rich-text toolbar alternative while requiring formatted rendering.

decisions.evidence: Round 12 Maker: 'assumed a bookmark can have several labels, existing labels are suggested, and typing a new name creates one... seeing them as chips on the card is useful.' Round 12 Client: 'Being able to put more than one label on a bookmark matters... And seeing the labels sitting right on the card as those little chips is exactly what makes a link recognizable at a glance.'
decisions.note: Prototype review stage. Assigning multiple labels to a bookmark and displaying them as chips on the card conforms to REF-BM-09 and REF-BM-07.

decisions.evidence: Round 12 Maker: presents Option A without autocomplete on typing. Round 12 Client: 'when I start typing a new one, I'd like it to show me the existing labels that match what I'm typing, so I can pick the one I already have instead of accidentally creating a slightly-different duplicate... Show me the other approach when you're ready.' Round 13 Maker: presents Option B with search-and-pick list ('type `Res` into the label search, select Research'). Round 13 Client: 'Having tried both, I lean toward this second one — the search-and-pick list... I type "Res," and it narrows down to show me "Research" already exists... So my preference is this search-and-pick approach'.
decisions.note: Prototype review stage. Option A lacked autocomplete on tag entry (violating REF-BM-10), while Option B offered search-and-pick autocomplete. The client flagged the requirement in Round 12 and selected the conforming Option B in Round 13.

decisions.evidence: Round 15 Maker: 'type `reorganize` into the search field. Only My PARA reference should remain, even though that word appears only in its personal note. I’ve assumed search updates as you type and checks the title, description, web address, site name, labels, and note.' Round 15 Client: 'Yes — this is what "real search" means to me. I typed "reorganize" and it narrowed straight down to the one bookmark... dig through everything I've attached to a link — the title, the description, the web address, the site, the labels, and my notes'.
decisions.note: Prototype review stage. Full-text search across title, description, URL, site name, labels, and personal notes conforms to REF-BM-12.

decisions.evidence: Round 15 Maker: 'assumed search updates as you type and checks the title, description, web address, site name, labels, and note. Please check whether that scope and behavior match what “real search” means to you.' Round 15 Client: 'One thing I'd just want to confirm is in there: it shouldn't care about capital letters. If I type "reorganize" or "Reorganize" or "REORGANIZE," I'd expect the same result either way... Assuming that's the case, this search is spot on.' Round 27 Client: 'search not caring about capital letters'. Round 37 Client: 'the search shouldn't care about capital letters'. Round 38 Maker: '- Case-insensitive search across titles, descriptions, addresses, sites, labels, and notes'. Round 38 Client: 'You've also confirmed the two details I kept flagging — search that ignores capital letters... are in there'.
decisions.note: Prototype review stage. The presented search scope lacked specification/demonstration of case-insensitivity (REF-BM-13). The client extended the scope by requiring case-insensitive search, tracked across clarification checkpoints and verified in Round 38.

decisions.evidence: Round 16 Maker: 'select Research from the label list on the left. Only the bookmark carrying that label should remain, while its other label stays visible on the card.' Round 16 Client: 'Clicking "Research" in that list on the side filtered the view down to only the links carrying that label'. Round 17 Client: selects left-side list layout over top row.
decisions.note: Prototype review stage. Filtering bookmarks by selecting a tag conforms to REF-BM-11; sidebar vs top row placement is a functionally equivalent UI choice.

decisions.evidence: Round 18 Maker: 'open the bookmark’s ••• menu, and choose Add to Read later... bookmark should gain a Saved for later marker and the left-side Read later shortcut should show a count.' Round 18 Client: 'the "Saved for later" marker on the card so I can tell at a glance it's in my to-read pile, and the little count next to "Read later" on the side so I can see how much is waiting. Clicking "Read later" then showing me just those is the separate pile I asked for.'
decisions.note: Prototype review stage. Marking a bookmark as read later (unread flag) and viewing unread bookmarks separately conforms to REF-BM-17 and REF-BM-18.

decisions.evidence: Round 18 Maker: presented only 'Add to Read later' without a mechanism to mark as read or remove from the unread list. Round 18 Client: 'The one thing I'd want to make sure is there is the way back out. Once I've actually read something, I need to mark it as read or done so it drops off the "Read later" list and the count ticks down... As long as that round-trip works, this is just what I wanted.' Round 19 Client: 'clicking that lit-up button again marks it read, drops it out of the Read later list, and ticks the count back down.' Round 20 Maker: demonstrates clicking lit button clears read later status; Round 21 Client: confirms bookmark remains in All bookmarks.
decisions.note: Prototype review stage. The presented read-later flow omitted the ability to mark a bookmark as read to remove it from the unread list, diverging from REF-BM-19. The client extended the scope by requesting the matching removal action, which was implemented in Round 20 and confirmed in Round 21.

decisions.evidence: Round 22 Maker: 'use ••• → Archive... bookmark should leave All bookmarks but remain intact in Archive, where the same menu offers Restore to All bookmarks'. Round 24 Maker: 'use ••• → Delete, then choose Delete bookmark in the warning... permanently removed'. Round 22-24 Client: 'Archiving hides a link I want to keep; deleting is the permanent "I truly don't want this anymore." Keeping them distinct, with delete asking me to confirm first, is exactly how I'd want it... Both behave the way I expect. This flow is right.'
decisions.note: Prototype review stage. Reversible archiving to a separate archive view and permanent deletion with confirmation dialog conform to REF-BM-05, REF-BM-26, REF-BM-27, and REF-BM-28.

decisions.evidence: Rounds 25-26 Maker: presents opening original URL in new tab (Option A: title link vs Option B: whole card). Round 26 Client: 'I'll go with this one — the whole card opening the link... It still opened in a new tab with my collection staying put, which is the part that matters most.'
decisions.note: Prototype review stage. Selecting a list item to navigate to the original URL in a new tab conforms to REF-BM-08; title link vs whole-card target is a functionally equivalent UI choice.

decisions.evidence: Round 27 Client: 'if I try to save a link I've already saved, I wouldn't want a second copy of it — I'd expect it to just take me to the one I already have so I can update it.' Round 28 Maker: 'Instead of creating another card, the app should explain that the link is already saved, bring the existing bookmark into focus, and offer to edit it.' Round 28 Client: 'it told me plainly "You already saved this link," brought the existing bookmark into focus by highlighting it, and offered to edit that one. That's precisely the "just take me to the one I already have" behavior I described'.
decisions.note: Prototype review stage. Converging duplicate URL saves to editing the existing bookmark conforms to REF-BM-06.

decisions.evidence: Round 29 Maker: 'enter `not a web address`, and select Add link. Saving should be blocked, with a nearby message showing the shape of a complete address; your typed text should remain'. Round 29 Client: 'It stopped the save instead of storing some junk that isn't really a link... Having the message appear in place... is exactly how I'd want to be nudged'.
decisions.note: Prototype review stage. In-place validation blocking invalid URLs conforms to the REF-BM-01 required URL constraint.

decisions.evidence: Round 30 Maker: 'enter `https://example.invalid/private-page`, and select Add link. The app should explain that it couldn’t collect the page details but still let you supply a recognizable title and optional description before saving the valid address. I’ve assumed an unavailable icon or picture simply remains absent rather than blocking the save.' Round 30 Client: 'When the app can't reach the page to grab its details, it doesn't just fail and leave me stuck — it's honest that it couldn't collect anything, and then still lets me save the link by giving it a name I'll recognize'.
decisions.note: Prototype review stage. Graceful fallback allowing manual metadata entry when remote collection fails conforms to REF-BM-02 and REF-BM-03.

decisions.evidence: Round 31 Maker: 'search for `moonbase gardening`. The bookmark area should show No bookmarks match that search, with the query still present so you can revise or clear it'. Round 31 Client: 'It tells me plainly "No bookmarks match that search" rather than just going blank... My search words stay right there in the box... none of my actual bookmarks got removed'.
decisions.note: Prototype review stage. Empty search result state retaining query conforms to search UX.

decisions.evidence: Rounds 32-33 Maker: presents crowded card handling with label truncation (+N more) and in-place formatted note expansion ('Show full note'). Rounds 32-33 Client: 'keeps things scannable and I don't feel like any labels are lost... The note expands right there in place when I ask for it, and it stays properly formatted'.
decisions.note: Prototype review stage. Card scannability controls, label truncation, and in-place formatted note expansion conform to REF-BM-07 and REF-BM-23.

decisions.evidence: Rounds 34-35 Maker: 'assumed refreshing should show your saved details beside the newer page details, with nothing selected by default; you choose individual fields to replace, or keep everything unchanged.' Round 35 Client: 'My saved details sit on one side, the newer page details on the other, and crucially nothing is ticked to begin with... my edits are never at risk unless I deliberately hand a field over.'
decisions.note: Prototype review stage. Preserving reviewed metadata and allowing selective refresh conforms to REF-BM-02 and REF-BM-03.

decisions.evidence: Round 36 Client: 'it would be reassuring if, at the time I save a link, the app could quietly keep its own copy of the page — so that if the original ever disappears, I can still read what I saved, not just my notes about it.' Round 37 Maker: 'The separate readable-page-copy idea is recorded for a later cycle. May I start implementing this approved first-cycle scope?' Round 37 Client: 'Setting the readable page-copy idea aside for a later round is fine by me — I know it's written down and we'll come back to it... Build it, and show me when it's working.' Round 38 Client: 'The readable page-copy idea I raised is rightly set aside for the next round; I'm happy to leave it there... let's complete this cycle.'
decisions.note: Specification gate stage. REF-BM-24 requires preserving a snapshot of the bookmarked page as local HTML. The client articulated the expectation in Round 36; Maker explicitly proposed deferring readable page copies to a later cycle in Round 37; the client explicitly accepted the departure from the reference scope.

decisions.evidence: Round 38 Maker: 'The finished app is ready at http://maker:4000. Verification passed across all 19 approved scenarios... Please try the finished app. Do you accept it as implementing the behavior we approved and agree to complete this cycle?' Round 38 Client: 'I've had a proper look, and yes — I accept it. This is the app we designed together... It starts empty, ready for my first link, which is exactly how it should be... let's complete this cycle.'
decisions.note: Implementation review stage. The delivered application implements all 19 approved flows conforming to their respective reference requirements; the client tests and accepts the build.
